findings.diagnosis: The prompt treats cuts that separate a finite verb (or auxiliary) from its immediate core complement as acceptable, but doing so often creates an entailment/confusion (missing predicate, orphaned argument) when pieces are translated independently.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_633','en_us_1116','en_us_1248','en_us_738','en_us_1113'] — these 5 sentences all show the policy cutting between a finite verb/auxiliary and the phrase that supplies its core complement or object, which the target kept together.
findings.type_predicate: a finite verb or auxiliary token is immediately followed (within 1–4 tokens) by a direct object, essential prepositional object, or a clausal/complement phrase

edit.text: Do not cut between a finite verb (including auxiliaries) and its immediately following core complement (direct object, essential prepositional object, or clausal complement).

findings.diagnosis: The prompt undervalues keeping numerals/quantifiers attached to their unit or measurement phrase; splitting them produces incoherent or contradicted short pieces.
findings.evidence: ['en_us_101','en_us_1255','en_us_741','en_us_998'] — these 4 sentences all had policy cuts that separated a numeral/quantifier from its unit/measurement (barrels/gallons, ¥ amounts, km2, 'three' + structures), and the offline target kept the numeral+unit intact.
findings.type_predicate: a numeral or quantifier token is immediately followed within 1–4 tokens by a unit, measurement phrase, currency symbol, percentage, or parenthetical unit

edit.text: Never cut between a numeral/quantifier and its immediately following unit or measurement phrase (including parenthetical units); treat the pair as a single atomic unit.
